subject: chemical-engineering
intro: Chemical engineering scales chemistry from flask to plant, leading to work designing reactors and refineries, treating waste, making new materials and teaching the discipline.

roles.title: Chemical Engineers
roles.what: Design chemical plant equipment and devise processes for manufacturing chemicals and products such as gasoline, synthetic rubber, plastics, detergents, cement, paper and pulp, applying principles of chemistry, physics and engineering.
roles.where: Material and energy balances, reaction engineering's PFR and CSTR design, separations with McCabe–Thiele, and the process-design-and-economics unit are the design work of the role, unit by unit.

roles.title: Environmental Engineers
roles.what: Research, design, plan or perform engineering duties in the prevention, control and remediation of environmental hazards, including waste treatment, site remediation and pollution-control technology.
roles.where: Mass transfer and separations — absorption, extraction, membranes — from unit 4 and the HAZOP and layers-of-protection safety unit feed directly into treatment-plant and pollution-control design.

roles.title: Materials Engineers
roles.what: Evaluate materials and develop machinery and processes to manufacture them to specialised design and performance specifications, working with metals and alloys, ceramics, glass, plastics and polymers.
roles.where: Process thermodynamics' phase equilibrium and the reaction-engineering unit's catalysis govern how polymers and alloys are made, while the heat-exchanger design topic sets the equipment they run in.

roles.title: Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses applying physical laws and principles of engineering to the development of machines, materials, instruments, processes and services — including chemical engineering — often alongside research.
roles.where: The NCEES FE Chemical knowledge areas this course follows, from balances through transport phenomena to process safety, are the accredited curriculum chemical-engineering departments teach and examine.
